name: Moped
description: A motor driven cycle with two or three wheels, pedals optional, whose power source provides no more than 2 brake horsepower (1,500 W) and can't propel it faster than 30 mph on a level road. The definition caps only combustion engines by displacement, so an electric two- or three-wheeler over the 750 W e-bike limit that stays within these bounds is a moped.

restrictions.rule: Two or three wheels, with or without pedals (O.C.G.A. §40-1-1(28))
Its power source provides no more than 2 brake horsepower (1,500 W) and can't propel it unassisted faster than 30 mph on a level road (O.C.G.A. §40-1-1(28))
Its drive works directly or automatically, without the rider clutching or shifting once it's engaged (O.C.G.A. §40-1-1(28))
An e-bike whose motor is over 750 W lands here if it stays within these limits; one over 2 brake horsepower or faster than 30 mph is a motor driven cycle
Riders must be 15 or older and carry a driver's license, instruction permit or limited permit of any class (O.C.G.A. §40-6-351)
Riders and passengers must wear protective headgear approved by the commissioner of public safety; an approved motorcycle helmet complies (O.C.G.A. §40-6-352)
Exempt from the motorcycle rules requiring eye protection and headlights and taillights on at all times (O.C.G.A. §40-6-350)
Exempt from registration and titling: no license plate
Has the rights and duties of any other vehicle's driver (O.C.G.A. §40-6-350)
Not allowed on limited-access highways or roads with a minimum speed limit above 35 mph
The Department of Transportation or a local government may ban mopeds from a road where they endanger the traveling public (O.C.G.A. §40-6-353)
